# Results — Study 103 (Turtle-Trader) on real daily tape

*Generated by [`examples/verify.py`](../examples/verify.py). The Turtle Donchian channel
breakout — go long on a break above the **20-day high**, exit on a break below the **10-day
low** (System 1); go short on a break below the 20-day low, exit on break above the 10-day
high — plus the 55/20 System 2 variant, tested across a basket of eight liquid trend-following
instruments (SPY, GLD, TLT, USO, UUP, QQQ, IEF, DBA), daily bars from 1993 to 2026-06-13.
Baseline: a random-entry control with matched trade count on the same bars. As-of **2026-06-13**;
fingerprints below confirm the exact tapes used.*

## System 1 — 20-day entry / 10-day exit (both directions)

The primary Turtle system. A long signal fires when the close exceeds the prior 20-day
high; position is exited when the close falls below the 10-day low. Symmetric for shorts.
Enter at the next day's open; exit at the next day's open after the exit channel fires.

| Arm | n trades | win-rate | mean (bps/trade) | HAC *t* |
|---|--:|--:|--:|--:|
| **Donchian breakout** | 12,159 | **57.7%** | **+327.7** | **+6.97** |
| Random entry (control) | 12,159 | 50.0% | +28.7 | +1.37 |

- The Donchian breakout earns **+327.7 bps/trade gross**, HAC *t* = **+6.97** — strongly
  statistically significant, clearing the ±2 inference bar by a wide margin.
- It **beats the random-entry control** by **+299 bps/trade** — the timing of the entry
  (after a new 20-day high) genuinely matters.
- The cross-over to the inference bar is unambiguous: signal is **REAL** on this arm.

## System 2 — 55-day entry / 20-day exit (both directions)

The longer-term Turtle system. Fewer but longer-duration trades.

| Arm | n trades | win-rate | mean (bps/trade) | HAC *t* |
|---|--:|--:|--:|--:|
| **Donchian breakout** | 7,763 | **61.4%** | **+601.0** | **+7.10** |
| Random entry (control) | 7,763 | 51.0% | +19.9 | +0.62 |

- Even larger per-trade returns; signal equally strong.

## Direction split — System 1, gross

| Direction | n trades | win-rate | mean (bps/trade) | HAC *t* |
|---|--:|--:|--:|--:|
| **Long only** | 7,568 | **70.4%** | **+850.6** | **+11.33** |
| Short only | 4,591 | 36.6% | **−534.3** | **−5.46** |

- **Long entries dominate**: the basket (equity ETFs, commodity ETFs, bond ETFs) has a
  structural upward drift over 1993–2026; going long on new highs harvests that trend.
- **Short entries lose**: a new 20-day low in an upward-drifting basket is usually a brief
  dip that recovers, not the start of a sustained bear leg. Shorting ETFs on 20-day lows
  in bull markets is a structural mis-match.
- The edge is **directionally split**: long breakouts are REAL; short breakouts are REAL
  in the wrong direction.

## Pre/post-publication split (System 1, both directions)

The full Turtle rules were published by Curtis Faith in 2003 (*Way of the Turtle*).

| Period | n trades | win-rate | mean (bps/trade) | HAC *t* |
|---|--:|--:|--:|--:|
| Pre-2003 | 893 | **65.1%** | **+703.4** | **+4.17** |
| Post-2003 | 11,255 | **57.1%** | **+302.7** | **+6.28** |

- The edge **decayed** after publication: −400 bps/trade, consistent with McLean-Pontiff
  (2016) post-publication arbitrage. But it did *not* vanish — the long-side drift premium
  persists.
- The 2008 crisis and 2020 COVID crash are major contributors to both the trend and
  the volatility of the post-period signal.

## Cost sweep (System 1, net, both directions)

At ~1.5 trades/ticker/year (about 0.7% annual turnover per ticker), per-trade costs are
negligible relative to the large per-trade returns:

| round-trip cost | net mean (bps/trade) | HAC *t* |
|---|--:|--:|
| 0 bps (gross) | +327.7 | +6.97 |
| 5 bps | +322.7 | +6.86 |
| 10 bps | +317.7 | +6.76 |
| 20 bps | +307.7 | +6.54 |

- A 20 bps round-trip cost barely dents the edge. The Turtle system is low-turnover by
  design: the large per-trade returns are the other side of holding through large moves.
- **The edge is not killed by costs at this frequency.** Whether it can be harvested at
  scale depends on position sizing and how much capital the signals can absorb.

## Verdict

- **Signal — REAL (long-only) / MIXED (both directions).** System 1 long-only: HAC
  *t* = **+11.33**; System 1 both directions: *t* = **+6.97**; System 2: *t* = **+7.10**.
  The long-side Donchian breakout captures a genuine momentum premium. Shorts in an
  upward-drifting ETF basket are structurally wrong-footed. The combined signal qualifies
  as REAL but is directionally heterogeneous.
- **Tradability — FRAGILE.** The edge is real but eroded post-2003 (−400 bps/trade),
  concentrated in large tail moves (2008, 2020), and short entries are reliably negative.
  Harvesting requires long-only implementation, a diversified futures basket (where shorts
  are valid), and patience through long drawdown periods. ETF-only, long+short is a trap.
- **Beats a random entry? — CONFIRMED.** Breakout mean = +327.7 bps vs random +28.7 bps;
  the timing of the entry (after a new 20-day high) carries genuine information.
